posts.content_md:
He doesn't read this forum and I'm pretty sure he doesn't check my web page often so I feel safe in talking about a new hologram I'm been trying to work on for my father for Fathers Day.

[It's detailed here](http://www.dragonseye.com/holography/2004_06.html#june18/) and I'll post pictures of the transmission and reflection copies as soon as they're made.

Here's a shot of the lit model

![Image](http://www.dragonseye.com/holography/images/present/2004_06/06180012.jpg)

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md: Cotton batten looks very promising for making clouds. In my holoflame experiments I've found that even without extreme precautions to prevent air currents it seems to show up pretty well in holograms. If it's any distance at all from the image plane, the blurring is sufficient to obscure all hint of its medicine bottle origins

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
> Cotton batten looks very promising for making clouds

Or nebulae

![Image](http://www.dragonseye.com/holography/images/present/09_2003/enterprisemodel.jpg)

![Image](http://www.dragonseye.com/holography/images/present/09_2003/enterprisefinal3.jpg)

I thought about using a transparency and making the background part of the hologram but then thought that an actual photo would be attractive. Based on my tests so far, I think it's going to work well.

posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md: It looks as if the plane is whizzing out through the clouds because the image plane is on the wings. Was this intentional? Anyway, great effect!

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
> It looks as if the plane is whizzing out through the clouds because the image plane is on the wings. Was this intentional? Anyway, great effect!

Thanks. Yeah, that was the intention. I didn't do anything to the model to make it look like the prop was moving so I thought I'd bring the plane farther forward and make use of the natural blurring of the parts that aren't in the film plane. This helps to make it look like it's in motion.
